sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त ।
त ऐक्षन्तास्माकमेवायं विजयोऽस्माकमेवायं महिमेति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta |
ta aikṣantāsmākam evāyaṃ vijayo 'smākam evāyaṃ mahimeti || 1 ||

lines.iast: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta
lines.deva: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त

lines.iast: ta aikṣantāsmākam evāyaṃ vijayo 'smākam evāyaṃ mahimeti

padaccheda.iast: brahma ha devebhyaḥ vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇaḥ vijaye devāḥ amahīyanta te aikṣanta asmākam eva ayam vijayaḥ asmākam eva ayam mahimā iti
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यः विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणः विजये देवाः अमहीयन्त ते ऐक्षन्त अस्माकम् एव अयम् विजयः अस्माकम् एव अयम् महिमा इति

translations.text: Brahman, it is told, won a victory for the gods. In that victory of Brahman the gods attained greatness. They thought: ‘Ours alone is this victory, ours alone this greatness.’

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the khaṇḍa: hearing ‘unknown to those who know, known to those who do not know’ (2.3), the dull may be misled: what exists is known by the means of knowledge, and what does not exist is unknown, like a hare's horn; so Brahman, being unknown, does not exist. The story is begun so that this may not be. For that Brahman is the ruler in every way, the supreme god even of the gods, the supreme lord even of lords, hard to know, the cause of the gods' victory and of the asuras' defeat: how should it not exist? The words that follow agree with this purpose. Or the story is to praise the knowledge of Brahman: by knowing Brahman Agni and the others became the foremost of the gods, and Indra even more. Or it shows that Brahman is hard to know, since even Agni and the others, of great splendour, came to know it only with trouble, and so Indra, though lord of the gods. Or the whole is for the sake of the meditations that are to be enjoined. Or it is to show that, apart from the knowledge of Brahman, the conceit of living beings that they are agents and enjoyers is false, as was the gods' conceit of victory.

Śaṅkara: Brahman, the supreme, as described. In the battle of the gods and the asuras it conquered the asuras, the enemies of the world, who break the bounds set by the Lord, and gave the victory and its fruit to the gods, for the stability of the world. The gods, Agni and the others, attained greatness. Not knowing that the victory and the greatness belonged to the Lord, the inner Self seated in themselves, all-knowing, who joins living beings to the fruit of every act, all-powerful, who wished the world to stand, they thought: this victory was won by ourselves, limited as Agni and the rest; this greatness, the fruit of the victory, of being Agni, Vāyu and Indra, is ours, not the work of the Lord who is our inner Self.

sanskrit.deva:
तद्धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर्बभूव ।
तन्न व्यजानत किमिदं यक्षमिति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad dhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādurbabhūva |
tan na vyajānata kim idaṃ yakṣam iti || 2 ||

lines.iast: tad dhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādurbabhūva
tan na vyajānata kim idaṃ yakṣam iti

padaccheda.iast: tat ha eṣām vijajñau tebhyaḥ ha prādurbabhūva tat na vyajānata kim idam yakṣam iti
padaccheda.deva: तत् ह एषाम् विजज्ञौ तेभ्यः ह प्रादुर्बभूव तत् न व्यजानत किम् इदम् यक्षम् इति

translations.text: It knew this (false thought) of theirs and appeared to them. They did not know it: ‘What is this venerable being?’

notes: Śaṅkara: Brahman knew the false view of those who looked on things with this false conceit, for it sees all, being that which directs the organs of all beings. Lest the gods be overcome through false conceit, as the asuras were, out of compassion for them and to favour them by removing it, it appeared for their sake within the range of the gods' senses, in a most wonderful, astonishing form fashioned by the greatness of its own power. yakṣam: a great being worthy of worship.

sanskrit.iast: te 'gnim abruvan jātaveda etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti || 3 ||

lines.iast: te 'gnim abruvan jātaveda etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti

padaccheda.iast: te agnim abruvan jātavedaḥ etat vijānīhi kim etat yakṣam iti tathā iti
padaccheda.deva: ते अग्निम् अब्रुवन् जातवेदः एतत् विजानीहि किम् एतत् यक्षम् इति तथा इति

translations.text: They said to Agni: ‘Jātavedas, find out what this venerable being is.’ ‘So be it’, (he said).

notes: Śaṅkara: the gods, not knowing it, afraid within and wishing to know it, spoke to Agni, who goes before them, Jātavedas, almost all-knowing: you are the brilliant one among us; find out in particular what this being is that stands within our sight.

sanskrit.iast:
tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti |
agnir vā aham asmīty abravīj jātavedā vā aham asmīti || 4 ||

lines.iast: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti
agnir vā aham asmīty abravīj jātavedā vā aham asmīti

padaccheda.iast: tat abhyadravat tam abhyavadat kaḥ asi iti agniḥ vai aham asmi iti abravīt jātavedāḥ vai aham asmi iti
padaccheda.deva: तत् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् कः असि इति अग्निः वै अहम् अस्मि इति अब्रवीत् जातवेदाः वै अहम् अस्मि इति

translations.text: He hastened to it. It said to him: ‘Who are you?’ ‘I am Agni’, he said; ‘I am Jātavedas.’

notes: Śaṅkara: Agni went to it wishing to ask, but stood silent near it, for want of boldness; the being spoke to him. Asked by Brahman, he answered ‘I am the well-known Agni, and Jātavedas’, praising himself as famed by two names.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमिति ।
अपीदं सर्वं दहेयं यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti |
apīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyaṃ yad idaṃ pṛthivyām iti || 5 ||

lines.iast: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti
apīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyaṃ yad idaṃ pṛthivyām iti

padaccheda.iast: tasmin tvayi kim vīryam iti api idam sarvam daheyam yat idam pṛthivyām iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मिन् त्वयि किम् वीर्यम् इति अपि इदम् सर्वम् दहेयम् यत् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति

translations.text: ‘What power is there in you, being such?’ ‘I could burn even all this, whatever there is on the earth.’

notes: Śaṅkara: in you who have such famed qualities and names. ‘I could burn to ashes all this world, the immovable and the rest.’ ‘On the earth’ stands for the rest too, since what is in the mid-region is also burnt by fire.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतद्दहेति ।
तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाक दग्धुम् ।
स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad daheti |
tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśāka dagdhum |
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti || 6 ||

lines.iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad daheti
tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśāka dagdhum
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti
lines.deva: स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति

padaccheda.iast: tasmai tṛṇam nidadhau etat daha iti tat upapreyāya sarva-javena tat na śaśāka dagdhum saḥ tataḥ eva nivavṛte na etat aśakam vijñātum yat etat yakṣam iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै तृणम् निदधौ एतत् दह इति तत् उपप्रेयाय सर्व-जवेन तत् न शशाक दग्धुम् सः ततः एव निववृते न एतत् अशकम् विज्ञातुम् यत् एतत् यक्षम् इति

translations.text: It placed a blade of grass before him: ‘Burn this.’ He went up to it with all his speed; he could not burn it. He turned back from there: ‘I could not find out what this venerable being is.’

notes: Śaṅkara: before him who had such conceit Brahman placed a blade of grass and said: burn this mere blade of grass in front of me; if you cannot burn it, give up everywhere the conceit that you are a burner. sarvajavena: with the speed of all his eagerness. Unable to burn the grass, ashamed, his boast broken, Jātavedas went back in silence from the being to the gods.

sanskrit.iast: atha vāyum abruvan vāyav etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti || 7 ||

lines.iast: atha vāyum abruvan vāyav etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti

padaccheda.iast: atha vāyum abruvan vāyo etat vijānīhi kim etat yakṣam iti tathā iti
padaccheda.deva: अथ वायुम् अब्रुवन् वायो एतत् विजानीहि किम् एतत् यक्षम् इति तथा इति

translations.text: Then they said to Vāyu: ‘Vāyu, find out what this venerable being is.’ ‘So be it’, (he said).

notes: Śaṅkara: the sense is as before. Vāyu is so called from blowing, going or carrying scent.

sanskrit.iast:
tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti |
vāyur vā aham asmīty abravīn mātariśvā vā aham asmīti || 8 ||

lines.iast: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti
vāyur vā aham asmīty abravīn mātariśvā vā aham asmīti

padaccheda.iast: tat abhyadravat tam abhyavadat kaḥ asi iti vāyuḥ vai aham asmi iti abravīt mātariśvā vai aham asmi iti
padaccheda.deva: तत् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् कः असि इति वायुः वै अहम् अस्मि इति अब्रवीत् मातरिश्वा वै अहम् अस्मि इति

translations.text: He hastened to it. It said to him: ‘Who are you?’ ‘I am Vāyu’, he said; ‘I am Mātariśvan.’

notes: Śaṅkara: Mātariśvan: he who moves (śvayati) in the mother (mātari), the mid-region.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमिति ।
अपीदं सर्वमाददीय यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti |
apīdaṃ sarvam ādadīya yad idaṃ pṛthivyām iti || 9 ||

lines.iast: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti
apīdaṃ sarvam ādadīya yad idaṃ pṛthivyām iti

padaccheda.iast: tasmin tvayi kim vīryam iti api idam sarvam ādadīya yat idam pṛthivyām iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मिन् त्वयि किम् वीर्यम् इति अपि इदम् सर्वम् आददीय यत् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति

translations.text: ‘What power is there in you, being such?’ ‘I could take up even all this, whatever there is on the earth.’

notes: Śaṅkara: ādadīya: I could seize it. The rest is as before.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतदादत्स्वेति ।
तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाकादातुम् ।
स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad ādatsveti |
tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśākādātum |
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti || 10 ||

lines.iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad ādatsveti
tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśākādātum
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti
lines.deva: स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति

padaccheda.iast: tasmai tṛṇam nidadhau etat ādatsva iti tat upapreyāya sarva-javena tat na śaśāka ādātum saḥ tataḥ eva nivavṛte na etat aśakam vijñātum yat etat yakṣam iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै तृणम् निदधौ एतत् आदत्स्व इति तत् उपप्रेयाय सर्व-जवेन तत् न शशाक आदातुम् सः ततः एव निववृते न एतत् अशकम् विज्ञातुम् यत् एतत् यक्षम् इति

translations.text: It placed a blade of grass before him: ‘Take this up.’ He went up to it with all his speed; he could not take it up. He turned back from there: ‘I could not find out what this venerable being is.’

sanskrit.iast:
athendram abruvan maghavann etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti |
tad abhyadravat tasmāt tirodadhe || 11 ||

lines.iast: athendram abruvan maghavann etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti
tad abhyadravat tasmāt tirodadhe

padaccheda.iast: atha indram abruvan maghavan etat vijānīhi kim etat yakṣam iti tathā iti tat abhyadravat tasmāt tirodadhe
padaccheda.deva: अथ इन्द्रम् अब्रुवन् मघवन् एतत् विजानीहि किम् एतत् यक्षम् इति तथा इति तत् अभ्यद्रवत् तस्मात् तिरोदधे

translations.text: Then they said to Indra: ‘Maghavan, find out what this venerable being is.’ ‘So be it’, (he said). He hastened to it; it vanished from him.

notes: Śaṅkara: Indra is the supreme lord; Maghavan, because he is strong. Brahman vanished from Indra when he had come near it: Indra's conceit of being Indra had to be removed more than any, so Brahman did not grant him even speech.

sanskrit.deva:
स तस्मिन्नेवाकाशे स्त्रियमाजगाम बहु शोभमानामुमां हैमवतीम् ।
तां होवाच किमेतद्यक्षमिति ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa tasminn evākāśe striyam ājagāma bahu śobhamānām umāṃ haimavatīm |
tāṃ hovāca kim etad yakṣam iti || 12 ||

lines.iast: sa tasminn evākāśe striyam ājagāma bahu śobhamānām umāṃ haimavatīm
lines.deva: स तस्मिन्नेवाकाशे स्त्रियमाजगाम बहु शोभमानामुमां हैमवतीम्

lines.iast: tāṃ hovāca kim etad yakṣam iti

padaccheda.iast: saḥ tasmin eva ākāśe striyam ājagāma bahu śobhamānām umām haimavatīm tām ha uvāca kim etat yakṣam iti
padaccheda.deva: सः तस्मिन् एव आकाशे स्त्रियम् आजगाम बहु शोभमानाम् उमाम् हैमवतीम् ताम् ह उवाच किम् एतत् यक्षम् इति

translations.text: In that very space he came upon a woman, greatly shining, Umā Haimavatī. He said to her: ‘What is this venerable being?’

notes: Śaṅkara: in the region of space where the being had shown itself and vanished, and where Indra was when it vanished, there he stayed, pondering what the being was; he did not turn back like Agni and Vāyu. Knowing his devotion to the being, Knowledge appeared in the form of Umā, as a woman. ‘Greatly shining’: of all that shines knowledge is the most beautiful, so the word fits. haimavatī: as one adorned with ornaments of gold (hema), that is, greatly shining. Or she is Umā herself, the daughter of Himavat; thinking that she, who is always with the all-knowing Lord, would be able to know, he approached her and asked what the being was that had shown itself and vanished.
